title: Documentation layout with sidebar and on-page TOC
description: A three-region documentation page: section navigation on the left, the article in the middle at a readable measure, and an on-this-page table of contents on the right that tracks the current heading. Includes search entry, version selector, previous/next links, and an edit-this-page link.
intent: Let readers find the right page, orient within it, and move to the next step without losing their place.
characteristics: collapsible section nav with the current page marked
article column held to about 70ch, code blocks may run wider
right-hand TOC of h2/h3 with current-section highlight
previous/next links at the end of the article
code blocks with copy buttons and language labels
interaction: TOC highlight follows scroll position (IntersectionObserver), clicking a TOC item moves focus to the heading; sidebar sections expand and collapse; search opens with a keyboard shortcut and a visible button.
responsive: Below about 1200px the TOC moves into a collapsible "On this page" disclosure above the article; below about 800px the sidebar becomes a drawer opened from the header.
accessibility: nav landmarks with distinct labels (site, section, on this page); aria-current="page" on the active link; skip link to the article; drawer traps focus while open and returns it on close.
limitations: Scroll-tracking TOC needs JavaScript; without it the TOC still works as plain anchor links.
Very deep hierarchies (more than three levels) overload the sidebar; split the docs instead.
